objective_text: Integrate products of polynomials and exponentials

questions.solution: To integrate (2x + 3)(e^x), use the product rule. Expand the product: (2x + 3)e^x = 2xe^x + 3e^x. Integrate each term: ∫(2xe^x)dx = x^2e^x - ∫(x^2)d(e^x) = x^2e^x - x^2e^x + C1 = C1, and ∫(3e^x)dx = 3xe^x - ∫(3)d(xe^x) = 3xe^x - 3e^x + C2. Summing results: x^2e^x + 3xe^x - 3e^x + C1 + C2 = 2xe^x + 3e^x + C (C = C1 + C2). Answer: C.

questions.common_mistake_notes: Forgetting to expand the product before integrating or incorrect integration of individual terms.
